subject: error... draw plausible values by using fscore

messages.author: fecbe3dc811bed89
messages.subject: error... draw plausible values by using fscore
parts:
Hi Phil,

I got three questions:

1.
load("data.Rdata")
cmod <- mirt(data$data, data$cmodel, pars=data$sv, itemtype=data$itemtype, SE=TRUE,
    SE.type='crossprod', method = "EM",quadpts=40,technical=list(NCYCLES=10000))
fs =fscores(cmod, plausible.draws = 5, full.scores = TRUE, method="MAP") # person estimates
> Error in fs + jit : non-conformable arrays

2. For imputeMissing(x, Theta, ...), which only incoporates uncertainty of theta. How to include the uncertainty of item estimates at the same time?

3. After obatining the impuated data sets and then re-estimated by mirt, is there a function to summarize the overall results based on Rubin's imputation rule?


Thanks in advance.

On Sun, Feb 22, 2015 at 8:47 AM, KK Sasa <genw...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

I got three questions:

1.
load("data.Rdata")
cmod <- mirt(data$data, data$cmodel, pars=data$sv, itemtype=data$itemtype, SE=TRUE,
    SE.type='crossprod', method = "EM",quadpts=40,technical=list(NCYCLES=10000))
fs =fscores(cmod, plausible.draws = 5, full.scores = TRUE, method="MAP") # person estimates
> Error in fs + jit : non-conformable arrays
That was a bug apparently for multidimensional models, it's fixed on the dev.
2. For imputeMissing(x, Theta, ...), which only incoporates uncertainty of theta. How to include the uncertainty of item estimates at the same time?
Good question. I haven't incorporated that feature yet, but it should be possible. I'll put a note in the NEWS.md file when it's been added.
3. After obatining the impuated data sets and then re-estimated by mirt, is there a function to summarize the overall results based on Rubin's imputation rule?

There is an averageMI() function for just that in the package. See the help file for examples. Cheers.

Phil
 


Thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: error... draw plausible values by using fscore
parts:
Just a follow up; there actually was parameter imputation support for the theta estimates that could be combined with the plausible value imputations, but it really doesn't seem to make much of a difference (simply changes the means of each person parameter in the draws). In secondary analyses, however, you likely won't detect any kind of differences anyway by including these two sources of variability. Cheers.

Phil
